No model accepts %1$s as an input, so every model must recognise it from your speech. A model can select a similar language instead and write correct sentences in the wrong language. The Turbo and the Large v3 models make this mistake least often.

Voice typing uses the language of the layout that you type on. The app tells the model which language to expect. This applies to a model that is built for one language, and to a multilingual model that accepts a language input. The model does not guess the language from a short clip.
The app tells this model to expect %1$s
This model detects the language itself

The sizes go from Tiny to Large. A larger model is more accurate, but it downloads slower and transcribes slower. The Medium and Large models use almost one gigabyte of memory while they run. A model that is built for one language is better at that language than a multilingual model of the same size. A single language model appears here after you turn on its language on the Languages screen.
This model handles all of your languages.

This model can translate speech to English.
It listens for your own words, keeps to the languages you dictate in, shows the words while it works on them, and takes up to two minutes at a time.
The app uses this model for the languages that you did not select a model for.
Only the gated models need this token, for example some Gemma models
No model is on your device yet. Download one below to use AI offline.

The best models are at the top, not the smallest ones. A model at the top writes better, but the download is bigger, the answer is slower, and it needs more memory. A gated model needs a Hugging Face account. Add your token above, then accept the licence on the model page one time.

These models run on llama.cpp, a second engine that runs any GGUF file. With Compute set to GPU, they use the GPU on a phone with a Snapdragon chip (an Adreno GPU), and the CPU on other phones. The models that read pictures download a second file, the projector, with them. The models above, which run on LiteRT-LM, stay the default. Each file is checked against the one the catalogue names before you can use it.
llama.cpp is an extra part of the keyboard that downloads when you first need it. Download it to use GGUF models.
llama.cpp is a separate download of a few megabytes.

You can import any LiteRT-LM model in a .litertlm file or a .task file, and any GGUF model, which llama.cpp runs. For example, a model that you converted yourself or downloaded in a browser. For a GGUF model that reads pictures, also select its mmproj file. You can select both files at the same time.

The GPU option is experimental. The app changes to the CPU automatically if the GPU does not start, or if a model stops during an answer. The GPU memory is much smaller than the system memory, so a large model frequently needs the CPU. Select CPU here if the GPU continues to fail. GGUF models use only an Adreno GPU, the GPU in Snapdragon chips. If a GGUF model already ran on the CPU, the GPU starts to work for it after the keyboard restarts.

NPU runs a model on the AI accelerator of your phone. It needs a build of the model for the chip of your phone, and only some models have one: %1$s. When Compute is NPU, Download gets that build. Other models, and a model that fails on the NPU, run as they do with GPU. The NPU build only runs on the NPU.

You can pin a model to each language in the list below. This is the one used for every language you have not pinned. Automatic picks the best downloaded model that covers the language you are typing in, which is usually what you want; choose a model here if you would rather always use the same one.

The GPU did not run Whisper on this phone, so the models run on the CPU. Select GPU to try again
Automatic keeps the models on the CPU on this phone. Select GPU to try them on its GPU
Getting the GPU version of whisper.cpp. Until it is here, the models run on the CPU

This applies to the GGML models only. The LiteRT models always run on the CPU. The GPU reads speech faster on phones with a Qualcomm Snapdragon chip (an Adreno GPU), mostly with the larger models, where reading a phrase takes the most time. Other GPUs (Mali, Xclipse, PowerVR) run Whisper through Vulkan, a separate download of about 30 MB, only when you select GPU: on many of them it is no faster than the CPU, so Automatic does not use them. The first use of the GPU after an install or update can take some seconds while the GPU prepares. If the GPU does not start, has not enough memory for the model, or stops during a phrase, the app gives that phrase to the CPU, and from then on the CPU runs the model on this phone. Select GPU again to try it again. Automatic keeps the Tiny models on the CPU, which is about as fast for them.
